answer: Hop-Depth Lock: a node's economic weight is divided by its sibling count at the parent, the nearest harbor where all N agents share one incoming edge. The sonnet rule enforces a fourteen-hop trace; any node failing the trace is marked sable and forced to recompute its full flow ledger. Each new sybil multiplies every existing sibling's transaction fee by its ordinal index, so the fifth spawn costs five times the first.
